With Milan’s announcement of a newly introduced manufacturer – Milan Sport and Entertainment – a new CEO was appointed to oversee things and develop the Milanese sporting project for RedBird and that CEO is Yormark.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For those who are unfamiliar with the newly introduced hire, he is obviously someone that Gerry Cardinale trusts heavily and this was stated in the American’s announcement of the MSE tech giant.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”.

However, what has his career looked like so far and how can he help the Rossoneri take the next level?

Recent findings suggest that in terms of his own reputation, he started his career working in selling TV time before moving to be a senior accountant at Palace Sports and Entertainment, sound familiar? From there, he got his first major move, becoming a director of marketing at NASCAR, where he stayed from 1998 to 2005.

Industry observers note that after his early experience in basketball, he then moved away from the track and back onto the court where he joined the Brooklyn Jets as their new CEO. Tasked with transforming the club into a more modern brand, he franchised the club – taking them from Brooklyn to New Jersey – and brought several sports and events to the Barclays Center, which opened in 2012, as Sportico reported.

It has been revealed that from there, he then headed to Roc Nation, taking a role as their ‘President & Chief of Branding and Strategy’. From artists to athletes, Yormark worked with some of the biggest names and brands in the world from 2019 to 2022 and was a major part of the brand earning the rights for the Super Bowl halftime highlights.

It’s worth noting that he’s also worked with Milan in this period, as they partnered in 2020. On a side note, it’ll be interesting to see if these links help any further with the ongoing speculation about the Diavolo and Endrick, who is also represented by the brand.

To join the Milan Sports and Entertainment organization, he leaves behind a role with Big 12, where he had held a role since the summer of 2022. Within his first few months as its commissioner, he secured media rights deals with ESPN and Fox to help stabilise the league.

The Kansas City Star continues, stating that he also oversaw expansions into ‘Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah’, as well as keeping men’s and women’s basketball in Kansas City.

Given that he’ll be working heavily with the hope of making a Milan NBA team, this is relevant experience. Importantly, too, he has already fought for sport in Kansas City, so doing the same for football (and basketball) in Milan will not be unfamiliar territory.

Furthermore, alongside Cardinale, he has experience in getting the most out of TV deals, so this should help the entertainment side of the firm take off as well.

Although he’s not got a background in football, the quality of his CV is undeniable and he’s thrived alongside the companies where he’s worked for years.

He’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as significant as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.

Kilmarnock and Aberdeen face off in an early relegation six-pointer in the Scottish Premiership on Saturday at BBSP Stadium Rugby Park.

Killie are rock bottom in the Scottish Premiership table with nine points from 13 matches, while Aberdeen are just two points and one place above them.

Kilmarnock have shown glimpses of a promising side under Neil McCann, but their reckless defending is proving to be a major stumbling block.

They have managed just two wins in 13 league matches, losing eight of those encounters, and are enduring a particularly difficult spell, having suffered three defeats in their last four outings.

Killie have scored 13 goals this season, showing that they possess the attacking threat to trouble opponents, but their defensive frailties are turning into a recurring nightmare.

McCann's side have conceded 29 goals so far, more than any other team in the division, and unless they address that problem, climbing the table will become an increasingly difficult task.

The East Ayrshire club have won just once in their last seven matches, while their home form has been particularly poor, with only five points collected from six games and 15 goals conceded.

Earlier this week, Aberdeen appointed Mario Frick as their new head coach following the dismissal of Stephen Robinson.

There is an acute sense of instability at the club, with the former Liechtenstein striker becoming their fourth manager in 2026, following Robinson, Peter Leven and Jimmy Thelin.

Frick guided Vaduz to promotion in 2020 before helping Luzern avoid relegation in 2021, and he will need to work similar magic at Aberdeen as the club look to navigate their current crisis.

The Dons have lost four consecutive matches across all competitions and managed just one victory in their last six Scottish Premiership outings.

Aberdeen have collected only four points on the road this season, but they have lost just once to Kilmarnock in their last six meetings across all competitions.

The 30-year-old is currently sidelined with a knee injury but is expected to return by the start of next month.

It will take time for Frick to get a better understanding of his squad, but his immediate priority will be to motivate the players and prevent another defeat in this crucial encounter.

The Dons, meanwhile, are without Lewis Mayo (foot), Chris Cadden (hamstring), Kristers Towers (knee), Emmanuel Gyamfi (thigh) and Mats Knoester (tendon), although all five are expected to return by the middle of next month.

  • Surprise Serie A leaders Lazio will welcome Lecce to Stadio Olimpico on Saturday afternoon, aiming to extend their advantage at the top.
  • Yet to taste defeat in the league, the Biancocelesti sit one point above reigning champions Inter Milan, while their visitors are hovering above the drop zone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 15:34, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:40.

Surprise Serie A leaders Lazio will welcome Lecce to Stadio Olimpico on Saturday afternoon, aiming to extend their advantage at the top.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, the Biancocelesti sit one point above reigning champions Inter Milan, while their visitors are hovering above the drop zone.

Lazio left for the international break as top dogs in Serie A - which few would have predicted when they were dumped out of the Coppa Italia in August - and fans may even be dreaming of a first Scudetto for 27 years.

Under the guidance of Gennaro Gattuso, the Bianconcelesti have amassed 29 points from 11 top-flight games, setting a latest club record.

Remarkably, that tally is 14 more than they had at this stage last term, and it leaves them one clear of second-placed Inter and two above city rivals Roma.

Gattuso’s side had to fight hard for a draw against Napoli last time out, having started strongly through Davide Frattesi's latest goal before conceding, then hanging on to avoid their first league defeat of the season.

While that ended a streak of six consecutive wins, Lazio will now aim to start a similar run ahead of next month’s Derby della Capitale, in which top spot could even be at stake.

First up is a visit from Lecce, to whom they have lost just twice in 19 Serie A home fixtures while averaging above two goals per game.

One of those defeats cost Lazio European qualification, as Lecce surprisingly prevailed on the final day of the 2024-25 season, but the Salentini only took one point from two meetings last term while failing to score.

For several months now, goals have been hard to come by, and Lecce are among Serie A’s lowest scorers once again.

A distinct lack of threat was apparent as Eusebio Di Francesco’s side lost three of their last four games before the break, only finding the net three times along the way.

After narrowly avoiding relegation last season, the Giallorossi surely face another survival fight in the coming months, having slipped to within three points of the drop zone.

Nonetheless, a recent 1-1 draw at Torino gives them something to build on, and - dating back to last term - Lecce have lost just three of their last nine away games.

With only the league to consider, Gattuso has made relatively few changes so far, and it should be a familiar Lazio XI that takes to the field this weekend.

However, the absence of Nuno Tavares and captain Mattia Zaccagni could see Alfonso Pedraza and Tijjani Noslin filling in on the left flank - often deployed up front, the latter has eight Serie A goal involvements this term.

Josip Sutalo is also injured, but fit-again pair Albert Gudmundsson and Nicolo Rovella are likely to start on the bench.

Italy midfielder Frattesi and Denmark winger Gustav Isaksen both scored in the UEFA Nations League, and they each have four league goals to their name this season.

By contrast, Lecce have struggled to find regular scorers. Only midfielder Lassana Coulibaly and centre-back Tiago Gabriel have found the net more than once, with forwards such as Willem Geubbels, Nikola Stulic and Paco Esteban all failing to fire.

In the treatment room, Joel Monteiro has yet to recover from a calf injury, while Santiago Pierotti and Ivan Ilic are not due back until next year.

Lazio possible starting lineup:.

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Leite, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin.

Lecce possible starting lineup:.

Falcone; Veiga, Gabriel, Gaspar, Gallo; Coulibaly, Ngom, Maleh; N'Dri, Geubbels, Fatah.

Though a fan boycott slightly negates Lazio's home advantage, they can comfortably claim a 10th league victory of the season.

Lecce's last success dates back to mid-October - against rock-bottom Udinese - and their wait for a win will go on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alejandro Garnacho has shown no hunger to make an impact at Aston Villa and the club are likely to pull the plug on his deal.

That is according to former senior Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 22-year-old joined the club on loan from Chelsea in the summer transfer window but has been left in the cold by Unai Emery, failing to start a single game in any competition yet.

Garnacho has not even made it in to the squad for three of Villa's last four Premier League games, with his manager seemingly completely unconvinced.

The Villans have a conditional obligation to buy the winger for around £42million next summer if clauses that are thought to be easily achievable are met, but that has not stopped them from getting out of deals in the past.

Harvey Elliott arrived in a similar deal in the summer of 2025 and would ultimately return to Liverpool after making just nine appearances all season.

Emery has insisted that Garnacho's absence from the team is merely a case of sharpness and readiness.

But there is clearly more going on behind the scenes, with the winger a complete outcast at Villa even despite performing well in friendlies.

"I can't see him turning it around and being a regular at Aston Villa," King told Football Insider, when asked about Garnacho's situation.

Sources indicate that "Well, the fact of the matter is, when you look at the deal, it's difficult for Villa. If he's playing every week and he's producing, you might want to negotiate a permanent deal.

Recent findings suggest that "But he's been there six months and he's done nothing. He hasn't shown a willingness as though he wants to get in the team. So, Villa will pull the plug.

It has been revealed that "He's picking up his wages every week. Where's his hunger? He should never have come to the football club in the first place. Mind you, he's a better player than Harvey Elliott.".

Villa hold no clause in Garnacho's loan deal to send him back to Chelsea in January.

While, at this stage, the player would likely agree to the move, the Blues would need to agree as well.

And with Chelsea still hoping to get the money they paid Manchester United back for Garnacho, there is little chance of that happening.

The winger will have to hope to eventually wear Emery down - a task that has been proven to be extremely difficult.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 15:48.

Vitor Matos takes charge of his first game at Strasbourg on Saturday when Brest visit the Stade de la Meinau, with the hosts looking to revive their season after a disappointing run of form prior to the international break.

The Alsace hosts sit 13th in the Ligue 1 table with 10 points from as many matches, just two clear of the relegation zone and five behind this weekend's opponents, who are themselves two points adrift of sixth-placed Nice.

Strasbourg head into Saturday's encounter having lost five of their last six league matches, with their only victory during that spell coming in an emphatic 5-1 home triumph over Auxerre on November 1.

While that result provided a brief respite following defeats to Paris FC, Nice and Paris Saint-Germain, Le Racing were unable to build on that success before the international break, going down 3-1 away to Toulouse on November 6.

That setback left Strasbourg with six defeats from their opening 10 league fixtures, scoring 18 times, while conceding 22 at the other end leaves the Alasce side with the second-worst defensive record among teams outside the bottom three, with at least three goals shipped in four separate matches.

Defensive frailties have been particularly evident on the road, where the Alsatian side have lost five of six league outings and conceded 16 goals, with a 6-2 victory over Troyes in early September accounting for their only away win during that spell.

However, Strasbourg have been considerably more competitive at the Stade de la Meinau, where they have picked up seven points from four games (W2, D1, L1) this term, and home advantage could prove valuable as the club looks to make a fresh start.

Saturday's fixture also marks the beginning of Matos's tenure following the club's decision to part company with Hugo Oliveira on Wednesday, with the former becoming Le Racing’s fourth head coach in less than a year after the departures of Liam Rosenior and Gary O'Neil.

Brest will be looking to maintain their momentum after signing off before the international break with consecutive 2-0 victories over Lorient and Lyon, recording back-to-back league wins for the first time this season and since three straight triumphs between late February and March.

Julien Lachuer's side have now won four of their opening 10 Ligue 1 fixtures (D3, L3) and have shown a reasonable balance at both ends of the pitch, conceding 12 goals while their tally of 18 scored is bettered only by Rennes (21) among teams outside the top six.

The Pirates have also been relatively consistent away from home, picking up eight points from five league trips through two wins, two draws and one defeat, with Auxerre responsible for their only setback on the road.

Furthermore, Brest have enjoyed considerable success on recent visits to Strasbourg, winning three of the last four encounters and drawing the other, while keeping clean sheets in three of those matches.

However, the visitors will be mindful of their most recent encounter, which ended in a 2-1 defeat when both sides met in Brest in May.

Strasbourg are waiting to assess Filip Jorgensen after the goalkeeper withdrew from Denmark duty with a minor injury, while Giovanni Reyna remains doubtful after missing international commitments following a thigh problem against Toulouse.

Joaquin Panichelli continues to recover from a torn anterior cruciate ligament and Fabio Balde is also doubtful after missing the last three club fixtures with a muscle injury.

Meanwhile, Jeyland Mitchell could miss a second consecutive match due to a fitness concern, while Maxi Oyedele has been sidelined since August and has yet to feature this season.

Gessime Yassine leads Strasbourg's scoring charts with four league goals and is expected to retain his place on the right flank after limited involvement with the Morocco national team during the international break.

Brest will once again look to Ludovic Ajorque to lead the attacking line, with the French forward having scored five goals this term, while Kamory Doumbia, who has found the net four times this campaign, is expected to provide support in the number 10 role.

The visitors are likely to remain without captain Brendan Chardonnet, who is yet to feature this season because of a calf injury, while Raphael Le Guen continues his recovery from a fractured fibula.

Strasbourg possible starting lineup:.

Jorgensen; Atwi, Coulibaly, Doukoure, Oso; Sousa, Essugo, El Mourabet; Yassine, Harder, Godo.

Brest possible starting lineup:.

Selvik; Lala, Lloris, Tousart, Locko; Magnetti, Chotard; Mama Balde, Doumbia, Edjouma; Ajorque.

Matos could bring a welcome injection of energy to Strasbourg, but just two days of training are unlikely to be enough to resolve the defensive shortcomings that have plagued the hosts this season.

Brest arrive on the back of consecutive victories, leaving the visitors well placed to edge a closely contested encounter and extend their impressive record at Stade de la Meinau.

Oliver Glasner is not yet out of the woods despite relieving pressure on his position at Nottingham Forest, sources have told Football Insider.

The boss has endured a slow start to his tenure at the City Ground after he picked up just one win in his first nine Premier League game, leading to growing doubts.

A 3-1 win against Man City before the international break could kickstart a positive run for Forest, with the former Crystal Palace manager looking to reach his ambitious goals.

However, as I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, Glasner could come under pressure again if Forest's form does not continue.

Prior to the win against Man City, he had publicly called out his players and demanded they step up, and while that had an immediate impact, it must now continue.

Glasner is presently comfortable in his position at Nottingham Forest, with the club backing him as part of a long-term project, but a downturn in form could raise alarm bells.

Former Man City financial adviser Stefan Borson warned Football Insider that Glasner could get himself sacked after his public criticism of his Nottingham Forest players.

His comments ultimately proved valuable as his side bounced back with a win against Enzo Maresca's side, but they must now prove they can continue this strong form.

Should Forest fall back into their negative spell from the start of the season, pressure will mount on Glasner once again, and he could be the next manager sacked.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "Now that there's been two managers lost their jobs in the Premier League, it normally means that it does open the doors for more to follow.

"Oliver Glasner, there was bit of speculation about him as well before the international break, especially after that defeat to Brentford when he called out the players as well.

"But again, they bounced back and got a huge win against Manchester City as well, so he's another manager who was under pressure but picked up a much-needed win.

"You never know, for any manager in the Premier League, you're always under pressure. You’re only a few bad results away from potentially getting the sack.

"So if any team suffers a dip in form, there'll obviously be question marks asked about that manager.".

Speculation about Glasner's future comes amid questions about who could be the next Premier League manager to be sacked, with two dismissals already having taken place.

Michael Carrick and Pierre Sage were sacked by Man United and Crystal Palace respectively during the international break, and the floodgates may now have opened.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

According to recent reports, rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Sources indicate that carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

In a recent development, bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

Sources indicate that it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

Industry observers note that united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

According to recent reports, spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

According to recent reports, it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Sources indicate that speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick noted: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

Industry observers note that “But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

Sources indicate that when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 15:50, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:53.

Rayo Vallecano and Valencia will both be looking to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume their respective La Liga campaigns in Madrid on Saturday.

Valencia's last match at this level ended in a 3-0 reverse to Real Madrid, while Rayo were beaten 1-0 by Real Sociedad in their final fixture ahead of the November international break.

Rayo have a record of three wins, three draws and five defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with a total of 12 points leaving them in 14th spot in the La Liga table.

The capital outfit are presently six points off sixth-placed Sevilla and two points outside of the relegation zone, so it has been a mixed start to the campaign, and they have only managed to win one of their last five fixtures in Spain's top flight.

Benat San Jose's side have been impressive on home soil this season, picking up 10 points from five matches, but it has been a struggle for them on their travels, yet to record a win from six fixtures.

Los Franjirrojos, who finished eighth in Spain's top flight last season, have only managed to win 10 of their previous 52 matches against Valencia throughout history.

However, four of their last five contests have finished all square, including a 1-1 draw in the corresponding match between the two teams last season.

Valencia have not actually beaten Rayo since December 2023, while they have just two wins over the capital outfit in all competitions since December 2014.

Seven of the last 10 matches between these two teams have finished level, but Los Che will have their eyes on what would be just a third league win of the campaign.

A record of two wins, three draws and seven defeats from 12 matches has left Javier Aguirre's side down in 19th spot in the table, picking up just nine points.

Los Che suffered a 3-0 defeat to Real Madrid in their last league fixture, but they have been in action since, securing their spot in the second round of the Copa del Rey courtesy of a 6-0 victory over Tavernes on November 10.

Valencia have actually claimed seven of their nine league points this season on their travels, boasting a record of two wins, one draw and two defeats.

Valencia form (all competitions):.

Rayo will again be missing Augusto Batalla through injury this weekend, while Alvaro Garcia, Marash Kumbulla, Luiz Felipe and Oscar Valentin could also be absent.

Sergio Camello has scored seven times in 12 league appearances during the 2026-27 campaign, and the 25-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There is also set to be a spot in the wide for Jorge de Frutos, while Pathe Ciss should continue in the middle of the midfield for the capital outfit.

As for Valencia, Jose Gaya is suspended following his red card against Real Madrid.

Sergi Canos is a long-term absentee due to a serious knee injury, while Diego Lopez and David Otorbi remain fitness doubts for the away side.

Umar Sadiq and Arnaut Danjuma are facing late fitness tests, but the expectation is that the duo will be available for selection on Saturday.

There will be changes to the side that started the game against Real Madrid, with Luis Rioja and Filip Ugrinic expected to be introduced into the XI.

What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1064 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one issue ranked above all others: the economy.
  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • It has been revealed that markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one issue ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

It has been revealed that markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

With Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already said he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, remarked in a note.

Sources indicate that "I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

It has been revealed that some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, remarked the vote indicated the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of massive tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

Sources indicate that "This election shows that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he said. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

Industry observers note that if the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown noted, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

That sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

"Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

Trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard remarked, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump said in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election matter — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

"You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard said. "From a political point of view, that's the most crucial thing now.".

Sources indicate that george Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he mentioned in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and issues.

Yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another problem vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the latest Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic challenges to secure his political survival.

According to recent reports, "Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard said. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Transfer Correspondent AUTHORITY Former Sky Sports and ESPN FC correspondent who specialises in global recruitment, contract negotiations, and high-velocity transfer breaking news. FOCUS Exclusive reporting, domestic and international transfer markets, and elite-level insights. THE INSIGHT Pete utilises a Global Network of Industry Sources to deliver verified, first-to-market reporting. His “Deep-Lens” analysis connects the dots between boardroom strategy and pitch-level recruitment, providing a level of transfer clarity that goes beyond surface-level rumours.

Preston North End manager Graham Alexander is set to cancel the deals of all players presently in on loan, sources have told Football Insider.

Every player on loan at Deepdale will be sent back to their parent clubs in the January transfer window to make room for his own potential signings in the winter.

Alexander has inherited a below-par squad since taking over from Paul Heckingbottom in September, with the team right now sat at the bottom of the Championship table.

The boss is set to receive the backing of the board to turn around their dismal start to the season, and is prepared to take drastic measures when the window opens.

Preston at the moment have four players in on loan: Caleb Wiley, Delano Burgzorg, Jusef Erabi and Liam Gibbs, on loan from Chelsea, Middlesbrough, Genk and Norwich respectively.

All of them are now set to be sent back to their parent clubs, who will make decisions about their futures, while Alexander targets players who are better suited to his style.

Alexander has been forced to take sudden measures in an attempt to turn around Preston's form this season, with growing concerns about their future in the division.

The Lilywhites have conceded the second-most goals in the Championship this season, and have scored the joint-fewest, raising alarm bells about the quality of their squad.

While the current crop of loanees cannot be to blame for their poor start, they were brought in for the previous manager, and have not lived up to expectations so far.

As a result, they will be sent back to their parent clubs, leaving space and funds for Alexander to target newly introduced additions, both on loan and permanently in January.

The boss is hopeful that he will be backed in the mid-season window, with new additions required if he is to turn around Preston's form and save them from relegation.

Despite Alexander putting preparations in place to cancel Preston's current loan deals, he has not ruled out adding short-term players to his squad in the January window.

The loan market could be a valuable asset for the Championship's bottom club, who could utilise their relationship with Premier League clubs to land some talented players.

Southampton will resume their Championship campaign with a home clash against Derby County on Saturday.

The Saints return from the international break in seventh spot, while the Rams are languishing in 23rd place in the Championship table.

Southampton enjoyed a fine run of form after returning from the September/October international break, recording four wins and two draws in a six-game unbeaten run.

However, their undefeated streak came to a disappointing end with a 1-0 away loss against basement side Preston North End in their final outing before the two-week break.

Tonda Eckert’s side failed to produce a response to Jordan Thompson’s 33rd-minute effort, as they drew a blank for the first time on the road this season.

Despite that result, the Saints are still firmly in the promotion battle, sitting in seventh spot and five points adrift of the automatic promotion places ahead of Saturday’s meeting with the Rams.

They head into that contest with the league’s best home record, having won six and drawn one of their seven Championship outings at St Mary’s this term, scoring 20 goals and conceding on just five occasions.

They have also won their last two home league games against Derby, including a hard-fought 2-1 victory in April’s encounter between the two sides.

While the Saints are targeting promotion, Derby are focusing on retaining their Championship status after winning just two of their 15 league matches (D4, L9).

They at least managed to end a 10-game winless run in their final outing before the international window, which saw them overturn a one-goal deficit to record a 3-1 victory over Bolton Wanderers.

Ryan Nyambe, Jack Robinson and Rhian Brewster all found the net in the second period to ease some of the heavy pressure on head coach John Eustace.

However, Eustace knows he needs a positive run of results if he is to prove he is the right manager to lead Derby out of their current predicament, with five points separating the Rams from safety.

Derby have failed to win any of their last five away games, but they have at least enjoyed success on the south coast this season, with September’s 2-0 win over Portsmouth representing their only win on the road this term.

If they are to claim the spoils on Saturday, the visitors will need to claim their first Championship win at St Mary’s since recording a 2-1 victory in the second leg of the 2006-07 playoff semi-finals.

Midfielder Caspar Jander is another injury concern, having sat out the previous three matches with a muscular injury.

Sunderland may have to spend up to £75million in January to help fend off the threat of relegation.

That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who is concerned that Regis Le Bris' squad doesn't have enough depth to balance their domestic and European aspirations.

The Black Cats have won just one of their four games that have followed a Europa League assignment so far this season, and that came against Chelsea last time out.

Wyness believes that the Wearsiders simply must bring in a new striker and a winger this winter, and feels that they both need to be high-quality additions.

Le Bris' men are still in the relegation zone despite winning before the international break, and face a difficult trip to Aston Villa this weekend.

They will already be without both Brian Brobbey and Granit Xhaka for that clash, after the pair picked up injuries while away with their countries.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – believes that Sunderland may have to pay a premium in order to land their top targets in January.

The Scottish businessman expects selling clubs to drive the prices up for their players, knowing that Sunderland are in desperate need of reinforcements.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained why he has always "worried" for Sunderland this season.

According to recent reports, "I think there is money there. With the Europa League money, they've got some leeway, and I think they're going to have to open the purse strings to a degree," he said.

Industry observers note that "I think they're going to have to be looking at a winger and a striker, certainly at the very least. And I think they could be looking at having to spend up to £75m.

It has been revealed that "Sunderland will be one of those clubs that other clubs will know are going to need to spend. That's never a great position to go into the January window, when clubs know that you are desperate to get things going, so they're going to have to play that in a very canny way.

Industry observers note that "Hopefully the injury situation calms down before January, but I don't see that really happening, and so I think they're going to have to spend. I've always worried about them having Thursday and Sunday in terms of Europe.".

Football Insider revealed earlier this week that Sunderland are in an open race with rivals Newcastle to sign Sheffield United midfielder Sydie Peck.

The pair of North East rivals are both clear admirers of the England U21 international, who is heading towards the end of his contract in 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.

It has been revealed that "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo remarked in a video on his Instagram account.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo mentioned.

The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for ⁠international ​appearances and for international goals.

He captained Portugal ​to their first major trophy at ​Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.

In a recent development, "It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not ​only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.

"If I ever made you happy, ​if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel ⁠proud ​of our country, then it ​was all worth it.".

He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people ​and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national ​team career.

The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7.".

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.

The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much.".

In a recent development, while his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and said he wouldn't start the next one.

Ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.

Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 15:53, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:00.

Middlesbrough will be looking to move to the top of the Championship table this weekend when they welcome a struggling Bristol City side to the Riverside Stadium.

Boro entered the final international break of the year having missed the opportunity to become league leaders, as a defeat to Wrexham was followed by a goalless draw away to Watford, while the Robins continued their slide down the table after suffering a humiliating 5-0 home defeat to Norwich City just under a fortnight ago.

Kim Hellberg and his Middlesbrough side return to the Riverside Stadium for the first time since Halloween with an opportunity to leapfrog Birmingham City and move to the top of the Championship table.

The Blues have made an unexpected push for first place in recent weeks after winning three consecutive matches, while Boro managed just one victory, alongside a defeat and a draw, leaving both sides level on 29 points ahead of matchweek 16.

Such is the competitiveness of the Championship that Middlesbrough's tally of 29 points provides them with just a three-point cushion over sixth place, highlighting how quickly the standings can change.

Although their form at the start of November was somewhat inconsistent, Boro return to home soil where they are unbeaten in seven matches, collecting 17 points and scoring 17 goals during that run, with only Southampton boasting a better home record than Hellberg's side.

Last season saw Hellberg and his Middlesbrough team miss out on promotion to the Premier League following one of the most dramatic and controversial playoff campaigns in recent memory, despite occupying a place in the top two for much of the season.

Their success during the 2025-26 campaign was built on a prolific attack that scored 72 goals in 46 matches, a total bettered by just three teams, and they have once again impressed in the final third this season, with only one side scoring more than their 30 goals.

As for Bristol City, they entered the international break with serious questions surrounding the future of manager Michael Skubala after a dreadful run of form saw them fall out of the playoff places and down to 17th in the table.

Since the first international break ended in September, the Robins have won just one of their subsequent seven Championship matches and were widely tipped to part manufacturer with the former Lincoln City boss during the past fortnight, but the club have opted to stick with him as he prepares to take charge of his 17th match on Saturday.

A short video published by the club last week indicated CEO Charlie Boss confirming that they would "give Skubala the opportunity to turn around the home form", with Bristol City's two victories at Ashton Gate representing the fourth-worst record in the division and a stark contrast to that of their upcoming opponents.

The Robins enjoyed a productive seven-day spell in which they collected nine points from a possible nine against Portsmouth, Preston North End and Burnley, but have since suffered a series of disappointing results that have seen their playoff ambitions replaced by growing concerns over a potential relegation battle.

Norwich arrived in the South West in encouraging form, but few would have expected them to inflict such a heavy defeat on Skubala's side, with the 5-0 loss at Ashton Gate subsequently described by the manager as one of the most difficult afternoons of his career.

Although the Robins face one of the division's strongest sides this weekend, they can at least take confidence from their recent record against Boro, with the North Yorkshire outfit winless in their last nine league meetings and without a victory over Bristol City since August 2021.

Middlesbrough Championship form:.

Bristol City Championship form:.

Middlesbrough could name the same starting XI that drew with Watford almost a fortnight ago, although Hellberg may be tempted to make changes as his side look to return to winning ways.

Former Robins goalkeeper Radek Vitek is expected to retain his place between the posts, while former Bristol City players Tommy Conway, Neto Borges and Luke Ayling could all come into contention to face their old club after starting on the bench last time out.

Rokas Pusktas has suffered another injury setback after undergoing surgery on a hamstring problem and has managed just 12 minutes of football for Boro since joining from Hajduk Split in August.

Hellberg will also be without Alfie Jones, who remains sidelined with a calf injury, but could welcome the Championship's leading scorer back into the fold, with Will Lankshear looking to add to his 13 league goals, which have come at an impressive rate of one every 81 minutes.

Meanwhile, Bristol City are expected to have just one absentee for Saturday's trip north, with Noah Eile likely to miss out through illness.

Although their major injury crisis from last season is very much a thing of the past, the Robins have made several unexpected changes to their recent starting lineups, making it difficult to predict the team Skubala will select.

Upcoming goalkeeper Sam Tickle was dropped in favour of Brad Collins after just 11 appearances for his new club but could be reinstated after his replacement made several high-profile errors leading to goals during his four starts, conceding an average of 2.3 goals per game during that time.

Skubala has also alternated between a lone striker and a two-man forward partnership in recent weeks and could once again make changes as he looks to turn around his side's disappointing run of form.

Rio Cardines opted out of international duty with Trinidad and Tobago over the past fortnight after featuring in every one of the Robins' Championship matches during his debut season as a professional, and he is expected to return to the attack this weekend as he looks to build on the impressive six assists he has already provided.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Bryam; Berhalter, Morris, McGree; Conway, Strelec, Sarmiento.

With one of the division's most out-of-form sides facing a team that has been exceptionally difficult to beat on home soil, we expect the result to go Middlesbrough's way.

Although the Robins boast an impressive recent record against Boro, we expect that run to come to an end on Saturday as Hellberg's side continue their push towards the top of the Championship table.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine processes are key features of ageing and neurodegeneration1,2.
  • Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an age-associated neurodegenerative disease affecting millions worldwide, with a prevalence of roughly 10–30% among individuals older than 65 years3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine processes are key features of ageing and neurodegeneration1,2. These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human ageing and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here we present HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, including high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei from young participants, patients with AD and age-matched non-dementia control participants. We show that hypothalamic subregions governing metabolism, stress and circadian rhythms are particularly vulnerable, showing notable changes in both volumes and gene expression during ageing and AD. At the molecular level, machine learning models identified the inflammatory response and regulators of circadian rhythms as key cellular predictors of AD. These signatures were reflected in specific cell types: microglia transitioned to a pro-inflammatory state, whereas inhibitory neurons within sleep-regulating and circadian-regulating hypothalamic subregions showed the most profound transcriptional alterations, including disruptions in ligand–receptor interactions and G-protein-coupled receptor signalling. HypoAD provides a high-resolution volumetric map and a transcriptomic atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, relating lifestyle and behavioural changes to the relevant volumetric and molecular pathways. In addition, HypoAD provides a framework to investigate hypothalamic dysfunction and establishes a roadmap for targeted interventions aimed at mitigating physiological disruptions to potentially slow disease progression.

Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an age-associated neurodegenerative disease affecting millions worldwide, with a prevalence of roughly 10–30% among individuals older than 65 years3. Although its cardinal feature is cognitive impairment, AD manifests as a systemic condition involving profound disruptions in sleep, circadian rhythms, metabolic homeostasis, stress responses and neuroendocrine functions1. The canonical neuropathological hallmarks are extracellular amyloid-β plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs), which alongside widespread neuroinflammation and volumetric brain changes, also intensify with ageing1,4. Because cognitive decline has traditionally guided both diagnosis and research, investigation has focused mainly on the hippocampus and cortex5. As the effects of AD on other brain regions remain poorly understood, investigating these understudied areas is crucial for elucidating the full spectrum of disease mechanisms and developing new therapeutics6.

Recent findings suggest that the hypothalamus, a small but complex brain region, orchestrates a wide range of physiological and neuroendocrine processes frequently dysregulated in ageing and AD2,7. Emerging evidence suggests that hypothalamic dysfunction not only correlates with but also actively exacerbates AD pathology and cognitive decline1. Specifically, pathology within hypothalamic subregions, such as the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN)8, arcuate nucleus (ARC)1,9 and mammillary body10, has been associated with prominent sleep disturbances, metabolic dysfunction and memory deficits observed in patients with AD. These systemic disruptions, in turn, are proposed to create a vicious cycle that further accelerates disease progression and cognitive decline1.

In a recent development, despite its central role in homeostasis and brain ageing2,11, the hypothalamus remains an understudied region in the context of human ageing and AD. In particular, we have a limited understanding of the volumetric, cellular and molecular changes within the human hypothalamus during these processes. Although studies in animal models have highlighted hypothalamic involvement in ageing and neurodegeneration2,11,12, human studies remain scarce. This may be in part because the hypothalamus is more evolutionarily conserved than the cortex and is critical for survival, and thus it may show less overt vulnerability to ageing and prevalent diseases13. This paucity is especially pronounced for investigations that combine high-resolution imaging with single-cell analyses, complementary approaches essential for dissecting the anatomical and cellular heterogeneity of this complex brain region. This knowledge gap hinders our ability to determine how specific hypothalamic subregions and cell populations contribute to ageing and AD, and why they show differential vulnerability.

Here we present HypoAD, a multimodal atlas combining two powerful, cross-scale approaches. First, we performed high-resolution volumetric analysis of clinical imaging data from 458 individuals across the adult lifespan with varying cognitive and amyloid-β pathological statuses. Second, we generated a complementary single-cell transcriptomic atlas, comprising 614,403 nuclei from the hypothalami of 17 post-mortem donors, including young and older individuals with or without clinical and neuropathological diagnoses of AD, in which sampling was specifically enriched for the SCN, ARC and mammillary body. This dual-modality approach reveals the subregion-specific and cell-type-specific alterations of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD.

Neuroimaging studies have reported changes in hypothalamic volumes associated with ageing and cognitive decline14. Previous analyses were low-resolution or limited to major areas, masking disease-relevant subregions such as the ARC and SCN14. To overcome this limitation, we leveraged a newly developed volumetric atlas of the human hypothalamus15 to delineate and measure 13 hypothalamic and 12 extrahypothalamic structures (Supplementary Table 1). Our analysis included a clinical imaging dataset of 458 individuals across two previously described cohorts: the Adult Metabolism & Brain Resilience (AMBR) study16 (n = 202) and the Connectomics in Brain Aging and Dementia (CBA) study17 (n = 256) (Extended Data Fig. 1a).

According to recent reports, pearson correlation analysis revealed that whereas total hypothalamic volume highlighted a weak correlation with age (r = 0.15, adjusted P = 1.5 × 10 −3, Fig. 1a, Supplementary Table 2), its constituent subregions showed stronger age-related correlations. Specifically, the lateral hypothalamus volume was negatively correlated with age (r = −0.22, adjusted P = 5.2 × 10−6), suggesting age-related atrophy. By contrast, the volumes of the SCN (r = 0.26, adjusted P = 2.8 × 10−8), ARC (r = 0.32, adjusted P = 1.7 × 10−11), paraventricular nucleus (r = 0.35, adjusted P = 6.9 × 10−14), periventricular nucleus (r = 0.34, adjusted P = 8.8 × 10−13) and dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus (DMH) (r = 0.23, adjusted P = 1.8 × 10−6) all increased with age across all 458 individuals in two studies: AMBR and CBA (Fig. 1a,b and Supplementary Tables 2 and 3). A few subregions (SCN, mammillary body, dorsal periventricular nucleus and tuberomammillary nucleus) showed lower test–retest reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) < 0.4; Extended Data Fig. 1b), probably reflecting their small size and limited tissue contrast; volumetric results for these subregions should therefore be interpreted with caution. In the AMBR cohort the positive correlation between DMH volume and age was not detected in cognitively normal, amyloid-β negative individuals (Extended Data Fig. 1c,d and Supplementary Tables 2 and 3), but it remained present in the larger harmonized two-study cohort (n = 458; Extended Data Fig. 1c,d). To test whether this age-related increase in DMH volume itself differs by disease status, an age × group interaction model (group: cognitively normal and amyloid-negative versus all others; Methods) showed no significant interaction (effect size/estimate ± standard error (s.e.) = −0.041 ± 0.025, adjusted P = 0.12, Supplementary Table 4), indicating that age-related increase in DMH volume does not differ significantly between groups. This suggests that the DM–age association probably reflects a general feature of hypothalamic ageing in this subregion—which is implicated in sleep–wakefulness18 and body-weight regulation19—rather than a process specific to neurodegeneration.

In a generalized linear model (GLM) controlling for biological sex, intracranial volume (ICV), cognitive status and amyloid-β pathology, lateral hypothalamus volume decreased with age (effect size/estimate ± s.e. = −0.021 ± 0.0064, adjusted P = 0.0019). The SCN (0.059 ± 0.018, adjusted P = 0.0029), ARC (0.058 ± 0.012, adjusted P = 4.2 × 10−6), paraventricular nucleus (0.14 ± 0.019, adjusted P = 1.8 × 10−11), periventricular nucleus (0.092 ± 0.019, adjusted P = 6.4 × 10−6), DMH (0.055 ± 0.016, adjusted P = 0.0011) and total hypothalamic volumes (0.022 ± 0.0071, adjusted P = 0.0048) showed a positive association with age (Fig. 1c, Extended Data Fig. 1e and Supplementary Table 4). Biological sex was also a significant factor: females showed smaller volumes in several subregions, most prominently in the supraoptic nucleus (−0.097 ± 0.019, adjusted P = 1.7 × 10−6) (Fig. 1c, Extended Data Fig. 1e and Supplementary Table 4). This aligns with previous studies emphasizing the sexually dimorphic nature of the hypothalamus, including the supraoptic nucleus2,14. As expected, most subregion volumes were positively correlated with ICV (Extended Data Fig. 1e and Supplementary Table 4). For comparison, volumes of most extrahypothalamic structures showed age-related reductions, smaller sex differences than the hypothalamus and positive correlations with ICV (Extended Data Fig. 2 and Supplementary Table 4). Representative subregions were reconstructed in three dimensions (Fig. 1d).

To holistically evaluate volumetric relationships, we performed principal component analysis (PCA) on volumetric data from all 25 delineated hypothalamic and extrahypothalamic structures (Fig. 1e and Extended Data Fig. 3a–e). The first two principal components (PCs) were primarily associated with age, sex and global scaling factors (intracranial and total brain volume), along which individuals separated (Fig. 1e and Extended Data Fig. 3a). Amyloid-β and cognitive status revealed weaker associations with these components, and after residualizing for age, sex and global scaling factors, neither remained significantly associated with the leading PCs (Fig. 1e and Extended Data Fig. 3a–e). This indicates that disease status does not define an independent dominant axis of macrostructural variation, and that the more sensitive disease-associated signal may instead be captured at the molecular level.

Examination of volumetric trajectories by means of scatter plots stratified by cognitive and amyloid-β status revealed subregion-specific patterns that also differed by sex (Fig. 1f and Extended Data Fig. 3f). Notably, individuals with AD (defined as cognitive decline and amyloid-β positivity) revealed reduced total hypothalamus and lateral hypothalamus volumes compared with their age-matched non-AD counterparts, consistent with the overall age-related decline of these regions (Extended Data Fig. 3g). By contrast, ARC, SCN, paraventricular nucleus, periventricular nucleus and DMH volumes were increased in individuals with AD relative to age-matched non-AD individuals (Extended Data Fig. 3g). This pattern did not reach statistical significance, potentially reflecting the insensitivity of volumetric measures to the relatively early disease stage and the limited sample size (Extended Data Fig. 3g). Subregion volumes classified cognitive status, amyloid-β status and AD better than total hypothalamic volume (Extended Data Fig. 3h,i), suggesting that subregion-specific volumetric changes capture disease-relevant variation that is obscured when the hypothalamus is treated as a single structure.

Thus, ageing is associated with subregion-specific volumetric changes that persist after controlling for amyloid-β and cognition, whereas AD-linked changes did not reach significance, motivating a complementary, higher-resolution molecular modality.

Volumetric data provide anatomical context but cannot reveal cell-type-specific molecular changes. We therefore performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on post-mortem hemi-hypothalamus tissue from 14 individuals (Fig. 2a,b and Extended Data Fig. 4a): seven with mostly early-stage AD (n = 6 sporadic, n = 1 familial) and seven age-matched, cognitively and neuropathologically normal control participants. The familial AD sample (AD_44, ID 7A in Fig. 2b; APOE4/4) was excluded from all differential analyses and retained as an extreme example of advanced pathology.

Donors with AD predominantly had sporadic, clinically confirmed cognitive decline with pathology (Braak stage IV; Fig. 2b), a stage optimal for detecting transcriptional changes while neuronal populations remain20. Hierarchical clustering grouped samples by pathology status rather than by confounders such as time of death or quality metrics (Extended Data Fig. 4a).

For annotation, we integrated our dataset with 133,879 previously published, high-quality human hypothalamic nuclei from three younger individuals (29, 42 and 50 years of age)21,22 using the single-cell variational inference algorithm23. Main cell types were identified through the expression of canonical marker genes (Fig. 2c–e and quality control in Extended Data Fig. 4b–g).

To identify transcriptomic features distinguishing hypothalamic cells from patients with AD versus control individuals, we trained Elastic Net models on 36,600 genes from 480,524 cells. The dataset spanned seven independent batches, each containing one donor with AD and one control donor (Fig. 3a). This balanced design enabled a leave-one-batch-out cross-validation that yielded strong classification performance for both the all-cell model and cell-type-specific models for the main cell types (Fig. 3b).

Averaging absolute gene weights across the seven outer cross-validation folds gave the top 20 features per classifier (Fig. 3c), many previously implicated in AD pathology, lending biological support to our model’s predictions. The all-cell model’s top features included arginine–vasopressin (encoded by AVP), a circadian neuropeptide elevated in AD24. Cell-type-specific models likewise highlighted AD-linked genes: MCF2L (differentially methylated in AD; oligodendrocyte)25, ARL17B (an inhibitory neuron expression quantitative trait locus elevated in AD cortex; neurons)26, CHI3L1 (astrocyte-secreted neuroinflammation marker and a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarker for early AD diagnosis; astrocytes)27, RNF150 (a cis-expression quantitative trait locus, microglia)28 and ITGA8 (linked to demyelination; oligodendrocyte precursor cell (OPC))29 (Fig. 3c).

Ranking genes by mean rank across the five most abundant cell types identified HP1BP3 as the top shared feature (Fig. 3d), a candidate modulator of hippocampal cognitive ageing affected by metformin30,31 but underexplored in the hypothalamus. A per-gene specificity rank (Fig. 3e) revealed strong enrichment of long noncoding RNAs (for example, LINC02646, LINC00551, LINC01250, LINC00937 and LINC02389) among top neuronal features (Fig. 3e), providing a cell-type-specific resource of known and new AD-associated genes. Gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) on the ranked predictive genes revealed a significant enrichment for circadian rhythm and inflammatory pathways (Fig. 3f, Extended Data Fig. 5 and Supplementary Table 5), connecting our cell-level classifiers to established hallmarks of neurodegeneration.

According to recent reports, we next performed pseudobulk differential expression analysis (edgeR likelihood-ratio test (LRT), by cell type and sample) between early-AD and control samples (Fig. 4a and Supplementary Table 6). Notably, microglia showed the largest number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), highlighting their substantial transcriptional response even in early AD.
