By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:05.

Chelsea will be looking to return to winning ways and strengthen their top-four credentials when they take on Leeds United in Saturday afternoon’s Premier League contest at Stamford Bridge.

These two teams served up a nine-goal thriller in the EFL Cup just a couple of months ago, with the West Londoners securing a 6-3 comeback victory in the third round.

Chelsea entered the international break on a sour note with just one win and three defeats to their name in all competitions, crashing out of the EFL Cup to Liverpool and enduring two setbacks in the Premier League.

The Blues responded to a surprise 2-0 home loss to Spurs by beating Man United at Stamford Bridge by the same scoreline, but they came back down to earth a fortnight ago with a disappointing 1-0 defeat to basement club Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

According to recent reports, five wins, one draw and four defeats have been posted in Xabi Alonso’s first 10 top-flight games for Chelsea, who sit fifth in the Premier League table and just two points behind Liverpool in fourth. However, Aston Villa down in 10th spot are only three points adrift of the Blues.

Having lost three of their first five PL away games for the first time since 2015-16 under Jose Mourinho, Chelsea should welcome this weekend’s return to Stamford Bridge where they have accumulated 10 of their 16 top-flight points this term, scoring the second-most home goals in the division (13).

The West Londoners have also won eight of their last 10 home battles with Leeds across all tournaments (D2) since a 2-0 defeat back in December 1999, though they were held to a 2-2 draw in this exact league fixture last season after letting a two-goal lead slip in the second half.

Following a five-match winless run that placed Daniel Farke under growing pressure, Leeds secured a much-needed 1-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road to enter the international break on a high.

A dominant second-half display was rewarded with a late strike from substitute Noah Okafor to help Leeds claim their third Premier League win of the season and rise to ninth in the table, six points clear of the bottom three and just two points behind Saturday’s opponents Chelsea in fifth.

Leeds are unbeaten across their last nine Premier League home matches (W5 D4) – their longest run at Elland Road in the top flight since an impressive 15-match streak between January and December 2001 – but they have only won one of their last eight league games on the road (D4 L3).

The Whites are now gearing up for four tricky away trips to Chelsea, Man City, Liverpool and Aston Villa, with Farke hoping that his side can showcase the same relentless character, commitment and unity shown in their win over Spurs as they attempt to improve their fortunes away from home.

Leeds head into this weekend’s contest seeking to end a 10-game winless run away against Chelsea in all competitions (D2 L8). However, having avoided defeat in their last two league meetings (3-1 at home, 2-2 away), the Whites will aim to go three consecutive games unbeaten against the Blues for the first time since between November 2000 and October 2001.

Leeds United Premier League form:.

Chelsea’s Reece James (knee), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle) all remain sidelined with injuries, but there is hope that Joao Pedro could be ready to return after missing the last four matches with a thigh problem.

Moises Caicedo (illness), Jorrel Hato (back) and Josh Acheampong (unspecified) are all doubtful, but goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez should be ready to start ahead for Mike Penders after recovering from a broken jaw to represent Argentina during the international break.

Morgan Rogers provided four second-half assists in the aforementioned EFL Cup win over Leeds in September, while Cole Palmer and Danny Welbeck both netted a brace. However, Welbeck may have to settle for a place on the bench once again, with Alonso possibly favouring either Estevao Willian or Pedro Neto in a central role alongside Rogers and Palmer.

As for Leeds, young forward Mateo Joseph is making positive progress in his recovery from a serious knee injury, but he remains sidelined, while midfielder Anton Stach is doubtful after missing the win over Spurs with a broken toe.

Farke will consider sticking with a two-man frontline of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, with Sean Longstaff and Ao Tanaka linking up with ex-Chelsea youngster Ethan Ampadu in midfield.

However, Noah Okafor will hope to force his way into the first XI after scoring as a substitute against Spurs, while Harry Wilson, Brendan Aaronson and Joe Rodon are also contenders to earn a recall, the latter of whom recently recovered from a long-term injury.

Chelsea possible starting lineup:.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Palestra; Estevao, Rogers, Palmer.

Leeds United possible starting lineup:.

Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Tanaka, Ampadu, Gudmundsson; Wilson, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin.

Chelsea have not been the same prolific outfit without the presence of Joao Pedro up front, and they could find it difficult to break down a robust Leeds backline without a natural focal point.

Despite only one of the Blues' last six Premier League matches seeing both teams score, we can see the net rippling at both ends on this occasion, with the hosts bouncing back from recent setbacks and edging to a slender victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Colin Chong has been massively underappreciated during his time as Everton's interim chief executive and real estate chief.

That is according to former Manchester City financial adviser Stefan Borson, who exclusively told Football Insider that he did an "amazing" job at keeping the Toffees afloat on Merseyside.

Everton have battled through building a fresh stadium, a change of ownership, continuous PSR alarm bells, and points deductions.

Chong joined Everton in 2016 during much of Farhad Moshiri's reign, spending the next 10 years at the club, but the latest enhancement confused many.

A Companies House upgrade revealed that Chong has been terminated as a director at Everton, with fans believing that this meant he was leaving.

However, it was revealed on Friday, 20 November, that Chong hasn't, and won't be, leaving the Toffees, but has simply just been removed from the board.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Borson stated that, despite the latest patch, the 61-year-old deserves more credit for his accomplishments.

"I always felt that the old management team, given the circumstances that they were working to, the very problematic situation they had with PSR at the same time as building stadium at the same time as the ownership issue..." he said.

"I always thought that the management team at that point had done an amazing job in keeping the show on the road.

"They got a lot of criticism at the time, but really, people don't realise how difficult that situation would have been for them. So many issues to deal with, as well as the day job of running a football club.

Industry observers note that understand Colin Chong hasn't - and isn't - leaving #EFFC. He has simply just been removed from the club's board. He took up the position when he was interim CEO, but Angus Kinnear now fulfils that role. Chong still playing an important role behind-the-scenes.

"And Colin Chong was the interim CEO during all that period before Angus Keneer took over from Leeds United a couple of years ago.".

A lot of what Chong has done seems to have gone under the radar on Merseyside, but the idea of him leaving has sparked a lot of praise.

He played a very vital role in the upkeep of Goodison Park, and once again in the building of the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Having become interim CEO in June 2023, Chong helped oversee things during great turmoil, including two PSR-related points deductions.

He had remained on the board following The Friedkin Group's takeover in December 2024, but that appears to have ended now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 16:04, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:37.

Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.

The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.

Lille head into the weekend in encouraging form after winning their last two league outings, beating Lens 1-0 before claiming a 2-1 victory away to Rennes prior to the international break, where Nathan Ngoy's second-half goal proved decisive.

Davide Ancelotti will be particularly pleased with how his side have rediscovered their rhythm after consecutive draws against Brest and Monaco derailed the Mastiffs' title charge, with the northern French outfit having lost just once in their opening 10 Ligue 1 fixtures (W6, D3).

Much of Lille's success this season has been built on their defensive solidity, with seven goals conceded representing the best record in the division, while five clean sheets leave them behind only Lorient (six) in that regard.

Les Dogues have also found the net in every league outing this season, although they have scored more than once in just 40% of their 10 top-flight matches, including two of their five fixtures on their own turf.

Nevertheless, Lille have been reliable at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, winning three of their five Ligue 1 games at the ground and avoiding defeat in the other two to boast the division's fifth-best home record.

Victory on Saturday would not only strengthen the hosts' position in the standings but also provide a timely confidence boost ahead of Wednesday's Champions League meeting with Bayern Munich, with the Mastiffs currently second from bottom in the league phase table after collecting just one point from their opening four continental fixtures.

Vicens will also have one eye on next Thursday’s home meeting with Lillstrom in the Europa League, where Lyon sit 13th in the 36-team table after picking up seven points from their first four matches.

However, the Spanish coach's immediate priority will be to get his new side back to winning ways following a 2-0 defeat at Brest in Lyon's most recent league outing, which came under interim boss Jorge Maciel following the departure of Paolo Fonseca for Sporting Lisbon.

That setback further highlighted Lyon's struggles on the road, having now lost their last three Ligue 1 away matches while conceding exactly two goals in each of those outings, with their only victory in five domestic trips this season coming against Toulouse on the opening weekend.

Nevertheless, a superior head-to-head record should offer the visitors some encouragement ahead of Saturday's contest, considering Lyon have won six of their last seven meetings across all competitions (D1) with Lille, including 1-0 victories in both league encounters last season.

Lille remain without Tiago Santos, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season after rupturing his cruciate ligament, while Hamza Igamane is also unavailable as he continues his recovery from an ACL injury, although a return is expected in December.

Ayase Ueda is doubtful after sustaining a plantar fascia injury, with the forward having resumed running but yet to return to full training, although Ancelotti previously suggested that the Japanese attacker could be available for this fixture.

Hakon Arnar Haraldsson has operated as a makeshift centre-forward in Ueda's absence and could continue in that position if the latter fails to recover in time, although veteran striker Olivier Giroud also provides an alternative.

Meanwhile, Lyon will be without Tyler Morton, who recently underwent surgery for an abductor problem, while Pavel Sulc is recovering from a meniscus injury and Mohamed Ouedraogo is sidelined for the remainder of the campaign after rupturing his cruciate ligament.

Lois Openda also remains unavailable as he recovers from a fractured fibula, although the forward is expected to return in the coming weeks, while Steeve Kango could be available after rejoining group training following a period under concussion protocol.

Lille possible starting lineup:.

Ozer; Ngoy, Nianzou, Alexsandro, Perraud; Bentaleb, Andre, Mukau; E Mbappe, Haraldsson, Diaoune.

Greif; Athekame, Niakhate, Bacher, A Vinicius; Tessmann, Bidstrup, Tolisso; Nuamah, Merah, Nakamura.

Lyon's recent dominance in this fixture makes the visitors difficult to dismiss, particularly with Vicens hoping to make an immediate impression in his first match at the helm.

However, Lille's superior defensive record, unbeaten home form and greater consistency in the league should give Ancelotti's side the edge, and we expect the hosts to secure a narrow victory.

#14863. Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?

Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fresh questions have emerged over Russia's return to world sport after figures reviewed by DW showed that only four of the 16 Russian weightlifters competing at this year's world championships underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing Agency (ITA).
  • Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.
  • By comparison, all 13 members of the North Korean team underwent at least one ITA test during the same period.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh questions have emerged over Russia's return to world sport after figures reviewed by DW showed that only four of the 16 Russian weightlifters competing at this year's world championships underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing Agency (ITA).

Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.

By comparison, all 13 members of the North Korean team underwent at least one ITA test during the same period. North Korea, like Russia, has a history of doping violations in weightlifting.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The ITA, which runs weightlifting's anti-doping program, told DW that it tested all 16 Russian weightlifters "ahead of their participation in the event." DW understands those tests were conducted in Ningbo, China, where the championships are being held.

In a power sport like weightlifting, performance-enhancing drugs are most beneficial during training, when athletes build strength and muscle mass in the months before competition. Some drugs, such as anabolic steroids, may be harder to detect by the time the competition comes around.

Rob Koehler, head of the athlete-led movement Global Athlete, called the lack of out-of-competition testing "absurd.".

"Out-of-competition testing is the backbone of anti-doping," Koehler told DW. "Everybody knows there's going to be testing at the event. But not everybody knows when they're going to be tested 365 days a year outside events. It's concerning that the ITA doesn't see this as a red flag.".

Marta Nawrocka, the ITA's spokesperson, said that Russian athletes were among the 10 most-tested nationalities in weightlifting this year. She also defended the fact that only two Russian weightlifters feature in the sport's highest-priority testing pool, saying inclusion is based on performance and risk profiles.

It has been revealed that "Russia's history of doping in weightlifting remains an important factor in the ITA's risk assessment and testing priorities," Nawrocka said. "Russian weightlifters remain subject to substantial testing activity.".

Koehler, though, is unconvinced.

In a recent development, "You simply can't treat Russia like any other country," he said. "It has to have more scrutiny. It has to have more testing. If you don't do that, you're undermining athlete confidence in the system.".

The International Weightlifting Federation did not respond to a request for comment.

Weightlifting was one of the sports most implicated in Russia's state-sponsored doping scandal, which came to light after the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics. It ranked second only to athletics for the number of positive cases identified by Canadian lawyer Richard McLaren in his 2016 report commissioned by WADA, the global anti-doping watchdog.

Industry observers note that the scandal led to dozens of Russian athletes being banned across numerous sports. RUSADA, Russia's anti-doping agency, has remained suspended for most of the past decade.

As a result, its Moscow laboratory cannot analyze urine and blood samples, meaning samples collected by the agency must be sent abroad for analysis under what WADA described as a "strict chain of custody.".

WADA said it continued to monitor RUSADA but had been unable to gain access to the country to review the agency's suspension because of the "ongoing geopolitical situation.".

It added that RUSADA had "collected thousands of samples … including hundreds from weightlifters" so far this year.

Industry observers note that "Given the history, WADA remains vigilant when it comes to Russia," James Fitzgerald, WADA's spokesperson, told DW. "We must ensure that no stone is left unturned when it comes to verifying that all the proper testing and other anti-doping activities are taking place.".

Despite being suspended, RUSADA still has the power to investigate and prosecute anti-doping cases involving Russian athletes, which critics find difficult to reconcile.

"It's a compounding problem that WADA is still giving them a free pass when it can't even get into Russia to see what they're doing," remarked Koehler, WADA's former deputy director general.

Sources indicate that "There's simply no oversight and no accountability. And quite frankly, I don't think there ever really has been.".

Critics also argue that ongoing questions over RUSADA's leadership and independence suggest that little has been fixed in the decade since the McLaren report.

Even the International Olympic Committee (IOC), whose president, Kirsty Coventry, supports the full return of Russian athletes, has acknowledged a "lack of confidence" over RUSADA's governance.

Nawrocka noted the IOC had "recently entrusted" the ITA with an expanded role within Russia in the run-up to the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, but did not explain what the role would involve or when it might begin.

Sources indicate that in April, investigative outlet The Insider reported that Veronika Loginova, the agency's head, was in a long-term relationship with an alleged FSB officer. The FSB, Russia's domestic security service, played a central role in covering up positive drug tests at the Sochi Games.

Loginova did not respond to questions for this article but dismissed the allegations at the time as "all this nonsense," writing in an email that she believed "sport exists separate from politics.".

WADA confirmed to DW only that its investigations unit was examining the allegations against Loginova and that the inquiry was ongoing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leeds United know that they will be able to secure a hugely lucrative fee for starting goalkeeper James Trafford in the coming years.

That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the 24-year-old’s valuation will have soared after his latest display for England.

Trafford was given the nod by Thomas Tuchel to start the Three Lions’ decisive Nations League game away to Spain last Sunday, and made some eye-catching saves.

Wyness believes that Leeds have no plans to sell the ex-Manchester City star any time soon, but know they will be in for a “handsome profit” when the time comes.

The Whites shelled out £45million to secure the gloveman’s services this summer, and he has already made that look like a bargain.

Trafford made six saves to help England to a surprise win in Madrid, including a stunning double stop at the death to help his team get over the line.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – believes that Leeds boss Daniel Farke will be delighted with the confidence boost that Trafford has just received.

The youngster is in a battle with Everton’s Jordan Pickford to be England’s number one, and may have now emerged on top, having been handed the start in the decisive game.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained how Leeds are relaxed over Trafford’s future right now.

“It’ll be difficult to double their money to make it £90m. I don't see him going for that. But I certainly see a good profit coming in for Trafford should he be sold,” he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that “Hopefully he won't be sold from Leeds’ point of view. Look, he did have a good performance. It's established great competition between him and the incumbent number one, Mr Pickford.

“Normally Pickford responds to this sort of thing by producing worldies for the next few weeks and reclaiming his position. Look, I think that Trafford is definitely a talent.

“He seems to have all the confidence. This will have done him the world of good. Farke will be happy with him coming back, full of confidence. There could be a handsome profit there in future.”.

Former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider earlier this week that winger Dan James is likely to push to leave Leeds in January if his gametime doesn’t improve.

The 29-year-old has played just 117 minutes of Premier League football so far this season, with Farke rarely trusting him on the pitch.

Brown outlined that the Welshman is “not happy” with his role at Elland Road, and isn’t prepared to sit on the bench for the remainder of the season.

The ex-recruitment man outlined that James’ athleticism still makes him a useful option from the bench, even if there are doubts over his ability at Premier League level.

Liverpool insiders are excited to see Conor Bradley back training but he will not be rushed back into match action anytime soon, sources have told Football Insider.

Bradley has been sidelined since he suffered a serious knee injury in Liverpool's goalless draw at Arsenal in January.

The 23-year-old right-back underwent surgery to repair both bone and ligament damage and has been working away in the background ever since.

Liverpool have struggled to solve their problems in his position ever since, with loanee Ronald Araujo now Andoni Iraola's first-choice on the right of the back four.

Bradley was pictured back on the grass earlier this week, but as I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, he is not close to a full return to action just yet.

Iraola is content with his right-back options as it stands, and so there is little rush to get the Northern Irish international back playing before schedule.

Bradley had just won his spot back in the Liverpool team under Arne Slot when disaster struck at the Emirates shortly after the turn of the year.

He remains widely tipped to make the position his own in the years to come, provided he can avoid more long-term injury problems that have plagued his short Reds career so far.

Industry observers note that speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "There’s no time frame as yet. Obviously it’s a huge boost to see him back on the training pitch and with some of his teammates. He’s not back in full team training just yet as he continues that recovery process.

"It's a huge boost for Bradley, first and foremost, that he’s back on the training pitch and also good news for Iraola. I think Liverpool will be careful with Bradley. They don’t want to take any risks with him. Obviously it will take him a number of weeks to regain full match fitness and sharpness, but it's good that he is back out there amongst his teammates.".

Araujo has made himself an Anfield favourite with his performances on loan from Barcelona at right-back in recent months.

Sources have exclusively revealed to Football Insider that Liverpool would like to sign Araujo permanently, as they have a £47million option to do so at the end of the campaign.

Barca sporting director, Deco, opened the door for him to join the Reds on a permanent basis with his comments this week, saying: "The most crucial thing for us now is seeing Ronald recovered, happy, enjoying himself and in a positive place.

"If he decides to stay, Liverpool have an option to make the deal permanent. They would also have to negotiate with him -- it's not just about paying the clause - but we would be happy for several reasons [if the deal goes through].

According to recent reports, "Firstly, because the move has worked out and because Ronald is happy and is able to continue his career successfully. We want players to succeed. Also, the money would not hurt, either.".
